Results.ReviewText: Excellent choice. Always have had a natural gas grill, and where I live now there's no natural gas. Wanted to try charcoal, but for everyday grilling, that is messy and tedious. I like the simplicity of the Q1200. I let it warm up for 15 minutes. Then experiment each time to find the right time to remove the food. I say experiment because its been at least 10 years since I used a gas grill. I am getting good at cooking burgers, but steaks are a challenge, however I will succeed. The Q1200 is really great at regulating the temperature, so the challenge is just based on my experience and skills. I say if I can master the timing of the grilling, then anyone can. I like that the Q1200 is lightweight, and can be transported if desired. If you are looking for a capable grill that can handle whatever you want to grill, the Q1200 is a perfect choice!
Results.Title: Maintains Temperature with Even Cooking: Foolproof

ClientResponses.Response:
Thank you for your feedback. We are so sorry to hear you are having an issue with the regulator. We are happy to help. If you are using your grill with the adapter hose to a larger 20 lb. refill/exchange LP tank, it sounds like your grill may be in a safety mode known as “bypass." What’s happening is that the regulator thinks there’s a gas leak, so it reduces the pressure. Follow these instructions to reset the bypass safety mode. This is also the way you would want to start your grill each and every time.
 
Open the lid
Make sure the control knob is in the off position
Turn your LP tank on all the way
Wait 60 seconds
Turn the burner to start/high (first position to the left)
Hit your igniter
Close the lid to preheat to 500-550°F
 
For troubleshooting purposes, we would suggest using your grill with a 14 or 16 oz. disposable LP cylinder as well. That will let you know right away if the issue is with the grill, or with the adapter hose/LP tank.

Our Care team will be reaching out to follow up. Please look for our outreach soon. Thank you!
